The paper explicitly states the Li/LiPON interphase width/thickness is ~76 nm. In the STEM-EDS section it says: "Based on the concentration gradient in Figure S5, the width of Li/LiPON interphase region was about 76 nm." Later, summarizing cryo-TEM/EDS: "the width of Li/LiPON interphase was about 76 nm" and "interphase with an average thickness of 76.4 nm" (Figure 2K). Thus an interphase thickness of 76 nm (nm units) is supported by the text and associated with the Figure 2 analysis (even though the alleged provenance cites Figures 2A–K pages 2488–2489, the statement also appears in the main text around those figures).

The paper’s cryo-STEM-EDS results explicitly report concentration gradients of phosphorus (P) and nitrogen (N) across the Li/LiPON interphase. In the section “Concentration Gradient across the Li/LiPON Interface” describing Figure 1D–G, it states that P and N are observed in the lithium metal region and that an EDS line scan shows both P and N increase across the interphase (with N extending deeper than P), i.e., clear concentration gradients. Since the extracted value’s 'value' is None (no numeric value specified) and the source provides only qualitative observation (no explicit gradient magnitude), recording the metric without a numeric value is appropriate.

The paper’s cryo-STEM-EELS section (Figure 3A–C; pp. 2490–2491) does discuss EELS spectra across the interphase and compares them to simulated spectra of Li2O and Li3PO4 (and Li3P, LiPON). Elsewhere, cryo-(HR)TEM/FFT and the conclusion explicitly identify SEI components including Li2O, Li3N, and Li3PO4 at the interphase. Therefore, the document does contain explicit signatures/identification of Li2O, Li3N, and Li3PO4 rather than omitting them. The extracted value of None is not supported.
